item.title: Added · 409/499 Illinois Street: Caffe Central (490 Illinois St; SF YIMBY, 2020-11-27, places…
item.description: Caffe Central (490 Illinois St; SF YIMBY, 2020-11-27, places UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois Street) had been missing and was added, confirmed via the cafe's own site, which publishes this exact address as a location. No opening date found (SF YIMBY reported the building open by Nov 27, 2020, so the cafe can't predate that). It is assigned to the 490-499 Illinois St record, whose sourced address is 490 Illinois St, not the neighboring UCSF Valley Center for Vision (west) record, a separate building about 60-100 m away across the street with an unresolved naming question. DataSF business registrations show no listing for Caffe Central at this address (only one at 460 16th St, presumably a different location of the same small chain), so, like Standard Deviant Brewing, it was a real tenant missing from the registration data. Source: https://www.caffecentral.com/490-illinois-street-mission-bay.
item.source: https://www.caffecentral.com/490-illinois-street-mission-bay

item.title: Milestone · Waterfront Park: Demolition, rough grading and shoreline improvements by… (May 2023)
item.description: Demolition, rough grading and shoreline improvements by DeSilva Gates substantially complete: the 2023 annual report (letter of Nov 22, 2024) says DGC 'substantially completed the Horizontal Construction Project, which includes demolition, rough grading, and shoreline improvements, between July 2021 and May 2023' and that 'In May 2023, CBC wrapped up the first phase of the Project's shoreline improvements, which included deep soil mixing (DSM), approximately 800 linear feet of seawall construction, installation of steel pipe piles for the future dock, riprap slope protection, and the storm drain outfall'; the 2024 annual report (Mar 2025) says the demolition, excavation, abatement, pile driving and deep soil mixing work 'was substantially complete in May 2023', yet still lists the Horizontal Construction Project among contracts underway at December 2024 and says no Phase 1 horizontal infrastructure is complete. The seawall and shoreline work runs along the Bay frontage where the waterfront open spaces are planned; the reports do not say which parts lie within Waterfront Park, The Point or the Prequel Park band, and the Phase 1 application describes early work as 'geotechnical improvements along the shoreline and in areas of fill'. None of this is landscape construction of the park itself (May 2023). Source: California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2024-11-22; California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2025-03; California Barrel Company / SF Planning (M-Files: 'Potrero Power Station Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment Applications'), 2020-10.
item.source: California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2024-11-22; California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2025-03; California Barrel Company / SF Planning (M-Files: 'Potrero Power Station Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment Applications'), 2020-10

item.title: Milestone · Chase Center: SF Board of Supervisors approves a separate… (~Jul 2020)
item.description: SF Board of Supervisors approves a separate, Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex (129-room hotel, 21 condos, ~25,000 sf retail) next to Chase Center at the northeast corner of the arena (Bisnow, July 2020); the article says the Warriors had not said when they hope to start construction, and no later status was found. Its relationship to this parcel (8722025) is not confirmed – see open questions. Not treated as this record's own status: Chase Center itself opened in 2019 and remains complete regardless of this separate, unconfirmed proposal. (~Jul 2020). Source: Bisnow (real-estate trade press), 2020-07.
item.source: Bisnow (real-estate trade press), 2020-07

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel E2 (block): Port Commission Resolution 20-07 authorizes… (~Feb 2020)
item.description: Port Commission Resolution 20-07 authorizes offering Brookfield a 99-year lease option on E2 at the appraised value of $5,000,000, below the $11,280,135 Down Market Threshold, in exchange for tying it to the Parcel A option and a faster Parcel A closing. Port documents give two adoption dates, February 11, 2020 (the certificate printed on the resolution) and February 25, 2020 (the Commission's minutes of that meeting), so only the month is shown; see open questions (~Feb 2020). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2020-02-07; Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2020-02-25.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2020-02-07; Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2020-02-25
